findings.reason: a second alias file forks the one alias owner the normaliser and every Unit-node write depend on, so unit canonicalisation drifts between the JT-60SA path and every other path.
findings.text: §4 proposes "a facility-unit alias file beside data_dictionary_unit_aliases.txt", a second alias file loaded into the one module-level registry; the existing file already IS the facility/data-source alias mechanism (its own comments read "malformed units used in the IMAS Data Dictionary" and "Case-sensitive aliases for MDSplus unit strings", i.e. per-source spellings), and the loader at imas_codex/units/__init__.py:48-53 loads exactly one definitions file into the single unit_registry — the honest change is to add the JT-60SA spellings to that file, not to fork a second one

findings.reason: naming merge_units_to_graph (and adding its file to the write paths, or calling it unchanged) is the difference between extending the one writer and creating a second one.
findings.text: §4's "EDAS signals are then linked to Unit nodes the way the MDSplus path links its signals" names no writer, and the owner of that write is merge_units_to_graph (imas_codex/discovery/mdsplus/graph_ops.py:321), which is already facility-generic, already reused by signals/parallel.py:3105 and static/workers.py:205, and already imported there to MERGE Unit nodes and create HAS_UNIT edges; §4's declared write paths (imas_codex/units/, imas_codex/discovery/signals/, tests/units/) exclude that owner file, so a worker following the plan will build a parallel HAS_UNIT writer inside discovery/signals/

findings.reason: the plan should extend the existing alias owner or state why it cannot, per the thin-wrapper rule.
findings.text: the facility-unit alias file is a thin layer whose only job is to forward spellings into the same unit_registry the existing file already feeds; the plan gives no justification for why the existing alias file or dd_unit_exceptions.yaml ("the single registry of DD-side unit bugs", imas_codex/units/dd_unit_exceptions.py:8) cannot be extended instead

findings.reason: folded into the duplicate_owner finding above; naming the owner there fixes it, so it needs no separate plan revision.
findings.text: §4's only un-named reuse is the HAS_UNIT link; the plan searched well elsewhere (it cites create_signal_source, normalize_unit_symbol, hybrid_dd_search and the shared rerank owner by file and line), so this is a single gap rather than a general one

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the plan composes existing machinery rather than spreading complexity across new wrappers; its only new code surfaces are an extension of create_signal_source (§3) and a rerank call into a shared owner (§8), each hiding more than it exposes.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §4 re-implements the alias-definition owner and, separately, risks a second HAS_UNIT writer beside the existing owner.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — this week's figures are public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; no section (§2 CLI runs, §3 grouping extension, §4 alias data file, §5–§7 existing CLI runs, §8 in-tool rerank) adds a public definition, a CLI option, an MCP view or a refusal family, so none owes a retirement or merge.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan cites most mechanisms it extends by name (build_enrich_claimable_predicate, create_signal_source, normalize_unit_symbol, hybrid_dd_search, claim_sources_for_candidates, the Jev rerank owner), but §4 describes the Unit link only as "the way the MDSplus path links its signals" and names no owner, and proposes a "facility-unit alias file beside data_dictionary_unit_aliases.txt" without citing the existing alias owner it duplicates.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §4's facility-unit alias file is a thin parallel layer over the existing pint alias mechanism, and the plan does not say why the existing alias file cannot simply carry the facility spellings.
